description:
## Goal

Represent operations implemented by the compiler/runtime as typed intrinsics rather than fictitious extern functions. One resolved intrinsic identity owns its exact input and result lanes, guard admissibility, fault behavior and lowering contract. Display names and linker symbols are never post-resolution semantic authority.

This ticket absorbs every valid requirement of fz-5xp.29 because the operator/comparison shims and the process-taking pseudo-externs are one indivisible model change. Leaving either family in extern syntax would preserve the compatibility path this cutover exists to delete.

## Correct model

Add one closed Intrinsic identity at the existing source/lowering boundary. Runtime-library declarations resolve it once and LoweredBody retains it with the validated semantic signature. Permission to declare an intrinsic or the reserved fz ABI comes only from the exact FunctionSource code owner recorded by World. Source spans and quoted metadata remain diagnostic data and cannot grant compiler-owned provenance. This ticket cuts ordinary interpreter and native execution onto that identity and exposes its typed guard-admissibility and Value-or-Fault contract. fz-tfn.62 then makes GuardDispatch consume the same identity while deleting guard reconstruction. Backend implementations may differ mechanically, but they exhaustively consume this one descriptor. The existing activation and transport facts retain the arriving evidence; intrinsic execution admits each arriving value against descriptor-owned runtime domains before unboxing or effects: any value, an exact scalar or binary kind, or a callable with an exact arity. World remains authoritative for richer erased relationships such as pid, cpointer and correlated resource contracts. Effect retention uses the activation evidence, so a possible dynamic fault remains observable without making a proven-safe comparison effectful.

The identity must distinguish exact operand/result lanes, integer div from integer-input float-result slash, widening equality from structural identity, mixed noncommutative lanes, and process/runtime effects. Kernel.spawn/2 and SpawnOpt take one integer min_heap_size byte hint, matching the existing documentation, fixtures, native lowering and runtime hook; replace the contradictory keyword() wrapper spec and generic opts name in this cut. Only explicitly guard-admissible intrinsic identities may terminate a reified guard helper. An arbitrary extern or same-spelled user function is never admitted by spelling or ABI resemblance. Intrinsic callsites enforce the exact semantic contract before fixed-lane lowering; only genuine extern declarations retain the existing contract-enforcement exemption. Provably incompatible lanes are one shared semantic diagnostic, while a mismatch not knowable until execution becomes IntrinsicFault::Domain rather than a backend panic or implicit coercion.

Intrinsic arithmetic preserves the existing language-value boundary: integers are signed i64 values and floats are finite. Integer overflow, negating i64 minimum, division or remainder by zero, and every nonfinite float result are IntrinsicFault, never wrapping values, debug-only panics or published infinities. Ordinary execution reports the fault through its existing process-failure boundary; fz-tfn.62 maps the same fault to the current ordered guard arms miss edge.

Migrate in this cut every current intrinsic wearing extern syntax: the arithmetic/comparison operator shims from fz-5xp.29 and fz_panic, fz_self, fz_send, fz_spawn, fz_spawn_opt, fz_make_ref and fz_make_resource. Generic extern handling must reject intrinsic declarations and never intercept them by name.

## Strategy and deletion

Reuse FunctionId, FunctionDefined and LoweredBody; do not add a purity registry, symbol side table, scheduler fact or second signature resolver. Replace the source declaration fiction with the typed intrinsic form, then delete ARITH_SHIMS, typed comparison symbol parsers, interpreter symbol interception, native name if-chains and obsolete runtime-symbol claims for names with no callable export. Retain real extern ownership and full ABI checking for actual callable symbols: fz_panic and the fz_op_rem_ff helper remain owned runtime exports used by intrinsic lowering even though their language declarations become intrinsic. Runtime shims made unreachable by typed inline lowering must be deleted.

Do not inline Kernel wrappers here; fz-5xp.20 owns that later optimization. Do not fold dispatch Region emitters; fz-5xp.22 retains its bitstring field-walk scope.

## TDD and acceptance

Red-first tests prove every declared intrinsic is claimed exhaustively on interpreter, JIT and AOT; no intrinsic can reach dlsym or generic extern marshalling; custom same-spelled functions remain ordinary functions; exact lane/domain behavior, widening equality, structural identity, integer slash, faults and process effects agree across ordinary execution doors. Prove the typed descriptor exposes guard admissibility and fault behavior without retaining a name-based guard path. fz-tfn.62 owns the atomic PatternGuardExpr/EntryDispatch cutover, lazy guard control, helper-miss propagation and function/case/receive guard parity. fz-tfn.67 retains ordinary native and/or selected-operand semantics. Prove unchanged artifacts and no extra work for unchanged/unrelated requests.

Update extern/runtime documentation. Run focused tests, all three doors, full library and fixture gates, formatting, check and strict Clippy. Remove probes and transition scaffolding. Fresh ticket-scoped cold adversarial review precedes one commit and close.
title: Give runtime intrinsics one typed declaration and semantic authority
